metadata.name: Measure Forest Change
metadata.description:
## Introduction
The Measure Forest Change pipeline maps forest loss, forest gain, and areas with no detected change using [Global Forest Watch (GFW)](https://globalnaturewatch.org/) data. It applies a minimum tree-cover threshold to the full selected area or separate thresholds to supplied subregions, and adjusts the 2000 baseline using loss recorded through the selected start year.
## Uses
Use the pipeline to see where forest change was detected, compare forest loss across regions, and summarize the area affected in hectares. These results can support forest monitoring, conservation planning, and reporting.
## Before you start
Leave Subregion boundaries blank to analyze the whole selected area with one threshold (15% if blank). For subregion reporting, supply a GeoPackage with one polygon layer and specify the field containing the subregion names. Use non-overlapping subregions. Features with the same name are combined. Paste the header `region, threshold` followed by one row per subregion with a value from 0 to 100. Separate rows with a backslash if the form uses a single-line field. Names must match the polygon attributes, including capitalization.

Choose Country or region to download by the selected area or bounding box. Choose Polygon and upload an area file to clip to a custom boundary, or choose Raster to use a raster extent. The analysis covers the selected area within available GFW coverage. Supplying subregions limits the analysis to their polygons within that coverage. Select a projected CRS that uses metres.

## Pipeline limitations
* **Geographic coverage.** The pipeline uses fixed boundaries for Guinea’s four natural regions. A custom analysis area limits which parts of those regions are included.
* **What tree-cover loss measures**. GFW detects canopy removal. The loss layer alone cannot distinguish permanent deforestation from harvesting, fire, or other disturbances.
* **Timing of forest gain.** The selected years define the forest-loss analysis. Forest gain comes from the GFW gain layer’s fixed source period (2000 - 2012).
* **Source data detail.** The resolution and classification accuracy of the source data limit how reliably small or fragmented changes can be detected.

View the [GEO BON STAC catalog](https://stac.geobon.org/) for the source collections.
